A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MAD by the same authors. The complete main texts, equations, figures, and appendices support comparison, including matching material moved or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy simulations, image-generation experiments, synthetic-data denoising, and Cryo-EM experiments, including appendix parameter sweeps.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds corrupted-image generation experiments, FID measurements in Table 1, and an inference-trajectory analysis.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same extended-score update, finite-difference approximation, and correction factor. However, v2's conclusion describes a limited scheduling variant that uses the extended score only during the last half of inference. Renaming the finite-difference parameter from δ to Δ does not change the method.

E1.justification: v2 adds CIFAR-10 with Gaussian corruption, FFHQ with Gaussian, shot/Poisson, and pixel-removal corruption, and synthetic shapes with 50% pixel removal. This substantially expands controlled noisy-training coverage beyond v1's synthetic corruption and Cryo-EM examples; the earlier clean-image demonstrations remain.

E2.justification: Standard-score inference remains the evaluated comparison method. Table 1 additionally measures noisy training data as a reference, not another method. Figure 18 inspects standard and extended inference trajectories; the cited training-time methods and posterior-sampling approaches are not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: v2 introduces clean-reference FID evaluation using 10,000 images, including training-data controls, across six corruption conditions. It also specifies 100,000 training samples for the new synthetic pixel-removal experiment. Figure 1's reported mixture variances change from 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 4 to 2, 0.5, 0.25, 0.1, 0.05.

E4.justification: Figure 18 adds a qualitative trajectory diagnostic addressing whether truncated standard sampling could explain denoising. New non-Gaussian experiments provide targeted corruption-robustness checks, and the conclusion briefly reports successful last-half-only extended-score use. Existing hyperparameter sweeps are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions describe consecutive random seeds for selected image grids, without reporting repeated-experiment uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v2's 10,000-image FID sample size is an evaluation setting, not a new repeated-run or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v1 contains no FID table. v2 Table 1 adds six conditions, including standard/MAD FIDs of 319.42/189.51 for synthetic Gaussian corruption, 147.47/77.15 for CIFAR-10 Gaussian corruption, and 257.42/101.12 for FFHQ shot noise. New image grids and trajectory results accompany these newly reported evaluations.

T1.justification: Definition 3.1, Lemmas 3.2, 3.3, and A.1, their proofs, and the correction-factor derivation are retained. Section 3's new footnote adds a limited mathematical generalization: replacing 1+γ with 1+γ/v makes the Dirac extended score match the score of a variance-v Gaussian.

C1.justification: The abstract and listed contributions retain the same central denoising and inference claims. The conclusion revises computational cost from roughly twice standard inference to at most twice, adding the qualified empirical claim that last-half-only use requires 50% additional computation.

C2.justification: v2 explains the regularization roles of a and b and acknowledges that their precise threshold relationship is undetermined. It interprets new corruption and trajectory results as evidence beyond Gaussian-noise removal or truncated sampling, and discusses unresolved adaptation to time-unconditioned and variance-preserving models.

D1.justification: v2 adds a MAD code-access link and documents the new synthetic pixel-removal construction, sample count, and reuse of training settings. Existing hardware and training disclosures remain. Conversely, Figure 1 loses its explicit mixture weights, means, and inference parameters, and several settings for the new natural-image experiments remain unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds related work on manifold-score decomposition, inverse problems, ambient diffusion, time-unconditioned generation, and classifier-free guidance. It clarifies distinctions from training-time denoising and posterior sampling while retaining the original research positioning. Bibliographic updates to retained works do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain. v2 expands parameter explanations, research positioning, the experimental overview, and the conclusion; adds a noisy CIFAR-10/FFHQ subsection; and reorganizes Appendix A.1–A.4 into Appendices A–D. These are localized expansions rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 1 and six experimental figures, redraws Figure 1, rearranges Figure 2, and enlarges or trims several image grids. The former Figure 5 parameter sweep moves to appendix Figure 12. A presentation regression is Figure 11's top/middle caption wording, which mismatches its side-by-side data/generated panels.

improvement.justification: v1 supports noisy-data generation mainly through visual synthetic and Cryo-EM examples. v2 adds controlled natural-image corruption experiments and clean-reference FIDs, substantially strengthening evidence for the central denoising claim; Figure 18 also probes the truncated-sampling explanation. Missing experimental settings, lost Figure 1 setup details, and a Figure 11 caption error temper reproducibility and presentation, but do not outweigh the substantial empirical improvement.
